content_html:
Peru is a country with an impressive cultural wealth, and its festivities are a vibrant display of its traditions, history and folklore. From colorful carnivals to religious festivals full of devotion, here are the most important holidays you should experience in 2025.

1. Cusco Carnival (March 1 to 9)

Known as the "Capital of the Inca Empire", Cusco celebrates this festival with parades, troupes, costume contests and lots of music. Attendees enjoy water and paint games, while the streets are filled with joy and typical dances.

2. Inti Raymi – Festival of the Sun in Cusco (June 24)

This ancestral ceremony, which takes place on the Sacsayhuamán esplanade, revives the Inca celebration of the winter solstice. More than 700 actors represent the cult of the god Inti with typical clothing and rituals in Quechua, transporting viewers to the splendor of the Inca Empire.

3. Festival of the Virgin of Carmen in Paucartambo (July 15 to 18)

Located in the Cusco region, this festival is famous for its traditional dances such as the “Qhapac Qolla” and the “Qhapac Chunchu”. For four days, the Virgen del Carmen is honored with music, processions and fireworks. It is one of the most authentic celebrations in the Peruvian Andes.

4. Independence Day of Peru – National Holidays (July 28 and 29)

The entire country dresses in red and white to commemorate the independence of Peru. In Lima the military parade and the Great Parade take place, while in other cities there are gastronomic fairs, cultural events and fireworks shows.

5. International Spring Festival in Trujillo (September – October)

This festival is one of the most important in northern Peru. It is characterized by beauty queen parades, the exhibition of Peruvian Paso horses and folk dances. It is a great opportunity to learn about Trujillo tradition and hospitality.

6. Lord of Miracles in Lima (October)

The Lord of Miracles is the largest religious procession in Peru and one of the largest in the world. During October, thousands of faithful dress in purple and accompany the image of the Purple Christ through the streets of Lima in an impressive demonstration of faith and devotion.

7. Feast of All Saints and Day of the Dead (November 1 and 2)

On this holiday, Peruvian families visit cemeteries to pay tribute to their loved ones with flowers, music and food. In some regions, such as Ayacucho and Cusco, special breads such as "wawa" and "caballo" de pan are prepared.

8. Fair of the Virgin of the Immaculate Conception in Puno (December 8)

Known as the "Mamita Candelaria", this festival in Puno is a prelude to the great festival of the Virgin of Candelaria in February. During the fair, there are masses, folk dances and craft fairs with typical products from the region.

9. Andean Christmas in Cusco and other regions (December 24 and 25)

In the Peruvian Andes, Christmas has a special touch with the Santurantikuy fair in Cusco, where artisans sell handmade nativity figures. Additionally, many communities celebrate with traditional music and dance, fusing Andean culture with Christian festivities.

Ready for your adventure then live the magic of cusco now.
